subject.title: plugins.code_safety: false positives on bundled plugin *.test.ts (env-harvesting matching whole-file string literals)

question: Should code-construct rules ignore non-executable string contents while retaining full-file scanning, rather than excluding test files or accepting the current false positives?
rationale: This changes a security heuristic’s detection boundary: test exclusion creates a coverage blind spot, while string masking must remain precise enough not to hide executable interpolation or payload-oriented detections.

options.title: Approve precise string masking
options.body: Adopt the active PR’s root-cause approach with full coverage and focused regressions for strings, templates, and preserved detections.

options.title: Keep the current heuristic
options.body: Accept the known critical false positives and document operator interpretation without changing scanner matching.

options.title: Exclude test files
options.body: Suppress the reported fixtures by filename at the cost of no longer scanning potentially executable test-named files.

recommendation.title: Approve precise string masking
recommendation.body: Adopt the active PR’s root-cause approach with full coverage and focused regressions for strings, templates, and preserved detections.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the scanner and are the strongest history-backed candidate to evaluate its intended detection contract.
